name: roll_check
description: Roll a skill check for a character: 2d6 plus the skill's level plus the attribute's modifier against a difficulty, 8 by default. An untrained skill counts as -1. Call it whenever an action is uncertain and a skill applies, such as climbing (Exert), spotting an ambush (Notice), or casting a spell under pressure (Magic). Higher difficulties mean harder tasks: 10 is skilled work and 12 or more is formidable. A total equal to or above the difficulty succeeds.

character.description: The name of the player character making the check.

skill.description: The skill id used, such as notice, sneak, heal, exert, or magic. A skill the character lacks counts as -1.

stat.description: The attribute whose modifier is added, such as int for an Int/Magic check or wis for a Wis/Notice check.

difficulty.description: The target number. 8 is routine, 10 is skilled work, and 12 or more is hard.

modifier.description: A situational bonus or penalty, such as -1 for poor tools or +2 for good preparation. Use 0 when none applies.

cause.description: What the check is for, in a few words, so the roll is recorded in the journal.

name: check_morale
description: Roll 2d6 against an NPC's Morale score to see whether they hold or break. Call it when an ally of the NPC is first downed, when half their side is down, or after a great reverse or a terrifying foe. A total higher than the Morale score means the NPC routs, retreats, or surrenders; a total equal to or lower means they stand. Player characters never check Morale.

name.description: The name of the NPC whose nerve is tested.

cause.description: What prompted the check, such as a companion falling or a monstrous foe appearing.

name: gain_xp
description: Add Experience Points to a character's XP total. Award about 3 XP for a successful session on the fast track, or 6 on the slow track. Fast thresholds are 3, 6, 12, 18, 27, 39, 54, 72, and 93; slow thresholds are 6, 15, 24, 36, 51, 69, 87, 105, and 139. When the total reaches the next threshold the tool records a note that the character may level up; it does not raise the level itself.

character.description: The name of the player character who earns the XP.

amount.description: How many Experience Points to award, usually 3 for a successful session.

cause.description: What earned the award, such as surviving an adventure or achieving a goal.

rate.description: An explicit track override. Leave it out to use the track chosen for the campaign.

name: gain_growth
description: Roll the character's background Growth table for a level's growth. Apply the result with improve_attribute, spend_skill_point, adjust_counter, or the appropriate skill or stat tool. Call it after level_up, once per new level.

name: level_up
description: Advance a character one level once their XP total has reached the next threshold (see gain_xp). For an NPC this applies the level's automatic gains at once. For the player character it applies nothing: the player makes the level's choices on the character sheet, so tell them to level up there and wait. The automatic gains are a rerolled hit-point total (level d6 plus the class constant and Constitution each level, keeping the old total plus one when the roll is worse), the class attack bonus, three skill points (four for an Expert or partial Expert), any Focus, art, and spell picks due, and a larger daily casting limit for a spellcaster.

character.description: The name of the player character who advances.

rate.description: An explicit track override. Leave it out to use the track chosen for the campaign.

name: spend_skill_point
description: Spend banked skill points to raise a skill by one level. The cost rises with the level: 1 point for level 0, then 2, 3, 4, and 5 points for levels 1 to 4. Level 2 needs character level 3, level 3 needs level 6, and level 4 needs level 9. Call it during downtime when the character trains or practices. Level 1 is ordinary competence, level 2 is the best in a city, and level 4 is the best in the world.

character.description: The name of the player character spending the point.

skill.description: The skill id to raise, such as notice or stab. It must be a skill of this rule set.

name: learn_focus
description: Spend one focus pick to learn a Focus at rank 1 or 2, or a nonhuman origin Focus with the GM's permission. The focus id must be a feature tagged focus or origin; rank 2 requires the character to already have the rank-1 focus of the same name. The character's class must allow the Focus. Only explicitly repeatable ranks can be learned again, such as Developed Attribute, Specialist, or Spirit Familiar rank 2; guide the player through choosing their distinct benefits. Call it at creation or during advancement when a focus pick is due. Fixed automated effects are applied when it is learned; choice-dependent benefits may need GM guidance.

character.description: The name of the player character who learns the focus.

focus.description: The id of a focus feature from the rule set, such as focus_alert or focus_alert_2. Use only ids tagged focus.

name: learn_spell
description: Add a spell to a spellcaster's spellbook. A High Mage learns High Magic spells; a Necromancer or Elementalist may learn High Magic or a spell of their own New Magic. The spell's rank (1 to 5) must not exceed the maximum spell level their class and level allow. Call it at creation or when a level-up grants a new spell. Learning takes 7 days minus the learner's Magic skill in days, with a minimum of 1 day, and needs a written copy or teacher.

character.description: The name of the player character learning the spell.

spell.description: The id of a spell feature from spells.json, such as spell_coruscating_coffin. Use a High Magic spell or one of the character's own tradition.

name: grant_package
description: Give a character one of the book's starting equipment packages. Creation already gives every character the kit the player chose, so use this only for a character who joined without gear, such as a promoted hireling. Do not use it to hand out an item the player says they have; those come from the story, from give_item, or from buy_item.

character.description: The name of the player character receiving the package.

package.description: The id of a starting equipment package defined by the rule set, such as a warrior or mage package.

name: set_ac
description: Set a character or NPC's total Armor Class for an art, spell, special adjustment, or a monster's printed AC. For tracked equipment this preserves the difference from calculated AC as an adjustment when equipment, Dexterity, or level later changes. Use equip_armor rather than this tool when armor or a shield is put on or taken off.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC whose AC changes.

ac.description: The new total Armor Class, normally between 10 (unarmored) and 19 (great armor).

name: create_magic_item
description: Create a permanent magic item after its magic-item project finishes. Charges the listed silver, then gives the character an item whose description records the item's powers. Use a weapon damage formula when the item is a weapon.

name.description: The character creating and receiving the item.

description.description: What the item does, in a sentence or two.

size.description: The item size, such as tiny, normal, large, or huge.

damage.description: Damage dice when the item is a weapon, such as 1d8.

name: choose_feature_choice
description: Record a structured choice a feature requires, such as the attribute for Developed Attribute or the skill for Specialist. The choice is validated against the feature and appears on the character's sheet.

pick.description: The pick's id, such as attribute or skill.

choice.description: The chosen stat, skill, or text.

name: prepare_execution
description: Prepare an execution attack with a carried weapon after a full minute of setup against a target that has not noticed the attacker. The preparation is lost if the target is spooked. Follow it with execute.

weapon.description: The carried melee weapon to use.

name: execute
description: Make a prepared execution attack against an unaware or helpless target. A melee execution hits automatically and deals the weapon's maximum damage; the target should then make the source's save with the attacker's combat skill penalty.

weapon.description: The weapon prepared for the execution.

name: grapple
description: Record a successful grapple after an unarmed hit and a won opposed Str/Punch check. Both characters carry the grappled condition: neither can move away, only unarmed attacks are possible, and the holder can hurt the target each round.

name: break_grapple
description: End a grapple after a successful opposed check or when the holder lets go. Both characters lose the grappled condition.

name: surprise
description: Mark a character or side as surprised. A surprised character loses their next turn and cannot attack until that turn passes. Use it when an ambush succeeds and the defenders did not notice the attackers.

name.description: The name of the surprised character.

name: total_defense
description: Spend a Main action on total defense. The character's Armor Class rises by 2 until the start of their next turn. Use it when a combatant gives up attacking to guard, and do not stack it with another total defense.

name.description: The name of the character taking total defense.

name: recover_after_rest
description: Apply the benefits of a good night's rest to a character: restore lost HP equal to the character's level, remove 1 System Strain, restore the day's spent castings, and return Effort committed for the scene or the day. Call it once after the party makes camp and sleeps. Injuries, Strain, and indefinite Effort beyond those amounts remain until healed or reclaimed by other means.

character.description: The name of the player character who rested.

name: prepare_spells
description: Prepare a spellcaster's set of spells for the day, taking 1 hour after a good night's rest. Each spell must already be known, and the number prepared is limited by class, tradition, and level: a full mage prepares 3 at level 1 and up to 12 at level 10, a partial mage prepares 2 at level 1 and up to 9 at level 10, and a dual partial mage uses the dual table with 3 at level 1 and up to 15 at level 10. Prepared spells stay prepared until a new set replaces them and are not lost when cast.

character.description: The name of the player character preparing spells.

spells.description: The spell ids to prepare, from the spells the character knows and, for specialist traditions, from their own tradition.

name: cast_spell
description: Cast a spell the character prepared. The spell must be in the prepared set and the character must have at least one casting left for the day; the cast spends one. Casting takes a Main Action, a free hand, and speech at conversational volume, and taking damage in the round prevents it. Full mages have 1 casting per day at level 1 and 6 at level 10; partial mages have 1 at level 1 and 4 at level 10. A good night's rest restores all castings.

character.description: The name of the player character casting the spell.

spell.description: The id of a prepared spell feature from spells.json, such as spell_coruscating_coffin.

name: commit_effort
description: Commit points of one tradition's Effort to a lasting art. Each tradition has its own pool and Effort from one cannot fuel another; only a character with that tradition or class can commit its Effort. Duration is scene (returns when the scene ends), day (returns the next morning after a good night's rest), or indefinite (returns only when reclaimed as an Instant action, and the art ends at once if the character is knocked unconscious or killed). Each commit costs 1 point unless the art says otherwise. High Magic, Necromancer, and Elementalist maximum Effort is 1 + Magic skill + the best Int or Cha modifier, minus 1 for a partial mage. Healer maximum Effort is Heal skill + the best Int or Cha modifier; Vowed maximum Effort is the chosen order skill + the best attribute modifier. All pools have a minimum of 1.

character.description: The name of the player character committing Effort.

tradition.description: The tradition whose Effort pool is spent: high, necromancer, elementalist, healer, or vowed.

amount.description: How many Effort points to commit, normally 1.

duration.description: When the Effort returns: at the end of the scene, the next morning, or only when reclaimed.

name: recover_effort
description: Return Effort committed for one duration: when a scene ends, after a good night's rest, or when the character reclaims an indefinite commitment as an Instant action. Give the same tradition and duration used when the Effort was committed so exactly the marked points are refunded. It does not restore Effort spent in any other way.

character.description: The name of the player character recovering Effort.

tradition.description: The tradition whose Effort returns: high, necromancer, elementalist, healer, or vowed.

duration.description: The duration of the commitment being released: scene, day, or indefinite.

name: add_strain
description: Add System Strain to a character. Strain is the body's toll from healing, magic, and hardship, and its maximum is the character's Constitution score. Call it after first aid, magical healing, or an exhausting effect, and say what caused it. A character at maximum Strain can take no more healing until some Strain is removed.

character.description: The name of the player character gaining Strain.

amount.description: How many points of System Strain to add, usually 1.

cause.description: What caused the Strain, such as first aid, a healing spell, or a hard march.

name: heal_strain
description: Remove System Strain from a character, such as 1 point after a good night's rest or more from a restorative effect. Give the cause so the change is recorded. Strain cannot fall below 0.

character.description: The name of the player character losing Strain.

amount.description: How many points of System Strain to remove, usually 1 per night's rest.

cause.description: What removed the Strain, such as a night's rest or a restorative draught.

name: first_aid
description: Treat a wounded ally after a fight. The healer rolls 1d6 plus their Heal skill (an untrained healer counts -1) and restores that many HP to the target, up to its maximum; the target then gains 1 System Strain, which counts against a maximum equal to its Constitution score. A target already at maximum System Strain gets no benefit from first aid.

healer.description: The name of the character giving first aid.

target.description: The name of the character being treated, who may be the healer.

name: restore_spell_slots
description: Clear a spellcaster's spent castings after a full night's rest, making the whole daily casting limit available again. It does not restore HP, System Strain, or Effort; use recover_after_rest for those.

character.description: The name of the player character whose castings are restored.
